doc.title: Willie J. Humphrey and Willie E. Humphrey Interview, 1959-03-15
doc.interviewee: Willie J. Humphrey and Willie E. Humphrey

title: Lewis Dumaine and Gus Metcalf
summary: Willie J. recalls Lewis Dumaine from the WPA band and recordings, and trombonist Gus Metcalf, a cousin of Bob Lyons taught by the grandfather.

story.theme_name: Trombonists: who they heard, admired and learned from
story.community_name: Talking trombonists: who played the slide and how

blocks.x: One night over at the Dream Room you were telling me about several old musicians, old time musicians. I remember saying I'd never heard of them before. I can't remember now who the names were even, but they said you remembered way back some of those... Oh, Gus Madcalf, I don't know if you... No, don't know about him. Oh, Gus, yeah, I don't know Gus.
I remember Lewis Dumain, yeah. Did you play with him too?
Yeah, I played with him. He had sort of... He was some kind of director in the WP band.
Oh, your brother made some records with him too, I believe.
Oh, that's right. The Red Onion Drag. And this Ann Cookie here I'm talking about. Oh, yeah, that's right. He made something. He certainly did.
Gus Madcalf, what did he play?
He played, I'll tell you, not my granddaddy taught him. He played trombone. He used to play a biotone and peck horn. That's right. He was pretty good.
That was Bob's cousin. Yeah, that's right.
Oh, Bob Lyons' cousin. That's the best.
